title: Переделанный салат и вечное противостояние  (The Remade Salad and the Eternal Rivalry)

segments.t: Welcome to Kukhnya Season 2, Episode 19. Max introduces the age-old rivalry between the dining room and the kitchen as an older female guest complains that her salad has too much oil. Max simply stirs the same plate and sends it back out until Chef Barinov spots the trick.

Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'Between the dining room and the kitchen.' Max brings out the contrast between 'hall' and 'both' in a few short words.
'Excuse me, I am listening.' Notice how Russian expresses 'forgive' and 'I'm listening' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Max answers right away.
'There is far too much oil in here.' Notice how Russian expresses 'there you go' and 'oil' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Please pass this along to the cooks.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'to pass on', while 'cooks' completes the thought.
'Have them remake the salad.' In Russian, the idea of 'let' flows naturally into 'salad' without extra filler words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'They asked to have the salad remade.' The meaning hinges on 'asked' working together with 'salad' in spoken Russian.
'Thank you for remaking it so quickly.' Max anchors the line on 'thank you', while 'to redo' completes the thought.
'Here you go, just the way you like it.' Chef Viktor chooses the respectful plural 'you' alongside 'to love' to keep a polite distance. Max answers right away.
'Well now, that is another matter entirely.' Max brings out the contrast between 'come on' and 'there you go' in a few short words.
'Are you out of your mind, tell me?' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'yes' and 'you' in a few short words.
'What is going on over here?' Notice how Russian expresses 'what' and 'happened' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
